projects.nameEn: Government School - Sayyida Aisha School in Obour City

updates.text: Excavation on this project encountered dense clay soil with high compaction and resistance, requiring the use of a heavy-duty jackhammer to break through the hard layers instead of conventional excavation methods. This posed an additional technical challenge given the project's tight schedule, requiring close coordination between crews to complete excavation on time without delaying subsequent activities.

Due to the unsuitability of the original clay soil for direct foundation bearing, soil replacement was carried out using clean coarse sand to a total depth of 50 cm, placed in two layers not exceeding 25 cm each, with mechanical compaction applied to each layer separately. Compaction quality was verified through a field density test, achieving a minimum compaction ratio of 98% — satisfying the requirements for safe foundation bearing prior to casting the blinding concrete.

Foundations were executed as a combination of isolated and combined footings, with an expansion joint incorporated at the column necks due to the building's total length of approximately 70 meters — a measure necessary to separate the structural mass and mitigate thermal expansion/contraction stresses. Standard footings were constructed to a depth of 50 cm, providing adequate support for the vertical loads transmitted from the columns.

Since the excavated clay soil was unsuitable for reuse, backfilling around the foundations and beneath the flooring was carried out using new clean sand. The backfill was placed in layers, with proper water flooding/saturation applied to each layer to achieve natural compaction of the sand and minimize the risk of subsequent settlement.

Column casting was carried out following completion of the foundations, ensuring continuous load transfer from the upper structural elements down to the foundations. Formwork (timber or steel) matched the design dimensions, with verticality checked using level and plumb line, and adequate concrete cover to reinforcement verified prior to casting.

Following completion of the columns, solid slab casting and staircases were executed, with reinforcement placed per the structural drawings, precise leveling, and formwork/props verified prior to casting to support the fresh concrete load and prevent deflection during construction.

Following completion of the structural elements, masonry works were carried out using two brick types: cement blocks in certain areas and hollow red clay brick in others, in accordance with the project's technical specifications. Proper bonding between units, verticality and horizontality checks, and door/window openings were maintained per the architectural drawings.

Plastering began with precise squaring of each individual space, followed by setting guide points and string lines in accordance with standard trade practice, ensuring wall straightness and consistent thickness prior to applying the plaster coat — achieving a level, uniform final finish free of distortion or waviness.

Waterproofing covered all areas susceptible to water or moisture ingress, specifically the roof, ground floor, bathrooms, and laboratories, along with any other zone exposed to potential water contact. Suitable materials were applied per surface type (bituminous membranes, liquid coatings, etc.), with proper drainage slopes maintained to prevent water accumulation and ensure long-term waterproofing performance.

Sanitary works on this project (Sayeda Aisha School) covered installation of plumbing systems for bathrooms and laboratories, in addition to water tanks (elevated and ground-level), ensuring proper water supply and drainage for all sanitary units in accordance with the approved engineering drawings and specifications.

Windows were fully executed as aluminum works, in accordance with the specified architectural dimensions and specifications, while interior doors were constructed from wood, with careful frame installation to ensure proper alignment, smooth operation, and secure closing.

Painting works covered interior and exterior walls, doors, and chair rails/wainscoting installed on the walls, following surface preparation (drying and leveling) prior to execution to ensure a uniform, defect-free final finish.

The building's exterior facades were finished entirely with Graffiato paint, a textured finish that provides a distinctive aesthetic appearance, helps conceal minor surface imperfections, and offers greater weather resistance compared to conventional smooth paint finishes.
